title: A power-torsion module has cokernel length bounded by its scalar kernel length
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $Q$ an $R$-module, and $f\in R$. Suppose that every $q\in Q$ is killed by some power $f^n$ with $n\geq1$. Write $Q[f]=\{q\in Q:fq=0\}$ and $fQ=\{fq:q\in Q\}$. If $Q[f]$ has finite module length $l=\mathrm{length}_R(Q[f])$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length], then $\mathrm{length}_R(Q/fQ)\leq l$; in particular $Q/fQ$ has finite length.

source.place: Tag 0BCR, lemma-affine-punctured-spec, converse proof, the length calculation for Q[f^n] and Q/fQ, lines 3383–3399.

proof.text: Put $K_n=\{q\in Q:f^nq=0\}$ for $n\geq0$, so $K_0=0$, $K_1=Q[f]$ and $K_n\subseteq K_{n+1}$. Set $T_n=f^nK_{n+1}\subseteq K_1$. Scalar multiplication gives a short exact sequence $0\to K_n\to K_{n+1}\xrightarrow{f^n}T_n\to0$: its kernel is exactly $K_n$ and it is onto the stated image. Any strict chain in $T_n$ is a strict chain in $K_1$, so its length is at most $l$, by [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Starting with $\lambda_0=0$, additivity [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] gives inductively $\lambda_{n+1}=\lambda_n+\mathrm{length}_R(T_n)<\infty$, where $\lambda_n=\mathrm{length}_R(K_n)$. The inclusions $K_n\subseteq K_{n+1}$ give $\lambda_n\leq\lambda_{n+1}$ by the same chain argument.

source.place: Tag 0BCR, lemma-affine-punctured-spec, converse proof: the paragraph beginning Set l_n and the two scalar-kernel exact sequences (lines 3383–3399); length additivity is Algebra Tag 00IV, lemma-length-additive.

proof.text: Write $C=Q/fQ$, let $\pi:Q\to C$ be the quotient map, and set $I_n=\pi(K_n)$ and $J_n=fK_{n+1}\subseteq K_n$. The restricted map $f:K_{n+1}\to J_n$ is onto and has kernel $K_1$. Moreover $K_n\cap fQ=J_n$: if $x=fy\in K_n$, then $f^{n+1}y=f^nx=0$, so $y\in K_{n+1}$; the reverse inclusion follows by multiplication. Thus the inclusion and quotient maps give short exact sequences $0\to K_1\to K_{n+1}\xrightarrow{f}J_n\to0$ and $0\to J_n\to K_n\xrightarrow{\pi}I_n\to0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] to both. All lengths are finite, and, writing $j_n=\mathrm{length}_R(J_n)$ and $i_n=\mathrm{length}_R(I_n)$, we have $\lambda_{n+1}=l+j_n$ and $\lambda_n=j_n+i_n$. Since $\lambda_n\leq\lambda_{n+1}$, cancellation of the finite integer $j_n$ gives $i_n\leq l$.

source.place: Tag 0BCR, lemma-affine-punctured-spec, converse proof: the paragraph beginning Set l_n and the two scalar-kernel exact sequences (lines 3383–3399); length additivity is Algebra Tag 00IV, lemma-length-additive.

proof.text: The power-torsion hypothesis gives $Q=\bigcup_{n\geq0}K_n$, hence $C=\bigcup_{n\geq0}I_n$, an increasing union. For any finite strict chain $N_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq N_s$ of submodules of $C$, choose $x_j\in N_j\setminus N_{j-1}$ for $1\leq j\leq s$. The finitely many $x_j$ all lie in one $I_N$; intersecting the chain with $I_N$ remains strict, witnessed by these same $x_j$. Consequently $s\leq\mathrm{length}_R(I_N)\leq l$. Taking the supremum of chain lengths, exactly as in [def-weil-pbc-module-length], proves $\mathrm{length}_R(Q/fQ)\leq l<\infty$.
